b1.texto:
Conditions are read in three passes.

**1. Obligations.** What each party has to do: «el importe restante **se abona** antes de la llegada».

**2. Deadlines.** Until when: «hasta el día quince», «en el plazo de diez días», «antes de».

**3. Exceptions.** They are introduced by **salvo que**, **a menos que**, **siempre que**, **excepto si**. Almost all of them take the subjunctive: «salvo que **se avise** con dos días».

A trick: look for the connectors first. If you see «salvo que», you already know the exception is coming, and the exception is usually the part that is hardest.
b2.f0.texto: How late can I cancel at no cost?
b2.f1.texto: You can cancel until the fifteenth.
b2.f2.texto: What happens if I don't show up?
b2.f3.texto: In that case the deposit is not refunded.
b2.f4.texto: Can you send me the receipt by email?
b2.f5.texto: I'll send it to you as soon as I receive it.
b4.e0.texto: The booking is confirmed when the deposit is received.
b4.e1.texto: The deposit is not refunded unless two days' notice is given.
b4.texto:
**Conditions** take the subjunctive: «salvo que», «a menos que», «siempre que». For example: «te lo cambio siempre que **traigas** el ticket».

**With «si» there are two worlds:**

- real: si + present, future → «Si **paga** el anticipo, la reserva **queda** confirmada».
- unreal: si + imperfect, conditional → «Si **pagaras** el anticipo, la reserva **quedaría** confirmada».

**Deadlines.** «Hasta» includes the day: hasta el quince means that the fifteenth still counts. «Antes de» excludes it. And «en el plazo de diez días» counts from today, not from tomorrow.
b5.f0.texto: The booking is confirmed when the deposit is received.
b5.f1.texto: The remaining amount is paid before arrival or at check-in at the accommodation.
b5.f2.texto: Cancellation is free of charge until the fifteenth of the previous month.
b5.f3.texto: From that date onwards, twenty per cent of the total is withheld.
b5.f4.texto: If the customer does not show up, the deposit is not refunded.
b5.f5.texto: It is advisable to keep the proof of payment for the whole stay.
b5.f6.texto: Any additional costs are charged at the end, unless something else has been agreed in writing.
b6.o0: Because «salvo que» is a condition and takes the subjunctive.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Correct: conditions and exceptions take the subjunctive.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Incorrect: negation does not change the mood.
b6.o2: Because it refers to the past.
b6.o2.refuerzo: Incorrect: «avise» is present subjunctive, not past.
b6.pregunta: In «salvo que se avise con dos días», why is the subjunctive used?
b7.frase: No se devuelve el anticipo salvo que ___ con dos días.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Incorrect: the indicative does not fit with «salvo que».
b7.o2.refuerzo: Incorrect: the future indicative is not used after «salvo que».
b8.frase: La cancelación es gratuita hasta el día quince.
b8.traduccion: Cancellation is free until the fifteenth.
b9.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «Cancellation is free until the fifteenth».
intro: Read some booking conditions and separate three things: what is binding, what deadlines there are and what exceptions are hidden. At B2 the hard part is not the vocabulary, but the nuance.
p.comprobar.consejo: The stem is irregular: compruebo, compruebas. And note «comprobar que» + indicative: it is a fact.
p.comprobar.glosa: to check that something is true
p.conservar.consejo: With documents, it means to keep them. Not to be confused with «conservar» a food.
p.conservar.glosa: to keep something so as not to lose it
p.el anticipo.consejo: Careful: this is not «anticipo» of time, it is money. Verb: anticipar.
p.el anticipo.glosa: the part of the price paid in advance
p.el comprobante.consejo: Also «el justificante». It is used to make a claim later.
p.el comprobante.glosa: a document that proves something was paid
p.el reembolso.consejo: Verb: reembolsar. In a contract it appears as «no procede el reembolso».
p.la condición.consejo: In conditions, almost everything important comes after a connector: «salvo que», «siempre que».
p.la condición.glosa: a requirement that has to be met
p.la estancia.consejo: Not to be confused with «la instancia», which is a document or an administrative level.
p.la estancia.glosa: the time spent in a place
p.los gastos.consejo: Careful: «gastos» in the plural usually refers to the extra costs: «gastos de cancelación».
p.retener.consejo: Irregular: retengo, retienes. In contracts: «se retiene el veinte por ciento».
p.retener.glosa: not to give back part of the money
p.salvo que.consejo: It takes the subjunctive: «salvo que llueva». It is one of the most frequent exceptions in contracts.
p.salvo que.glosa: except if such a thing happens
p.presento.consejo: From «presentar». «Presentarse» means to appear somewhere, to show up at an event.
p.envío.consejo: From «enviar», to send. The accent on «í» separates the vowels «i» and «o».
p.confirmada.consejo: From «confirmar». The feminine «-a» agrees with «reserva», which is feminine.
p.importe.consejo: A sum of money to pay. It comes from «importar», which here means to cost.
p.restante.consejo: From «resto», the rest. It describes what is still left to pay.
p.abona.consejo: From «abonar», to pay or credit a sum. The «-a» ending is for «usted» or «él».
p.recepción.consejo: From «recibir», to receive. In a hotel it is the front desk where you arrive.
p.cancelación.consejo: From «cancelar», to cancel. The «-ción» ending turns the verb into a noun.
p.gratuita.consejo: From «gratis», free. Feminine form, agreeing with «cancelación».
p.retiene.consejo: From «tener», to have, with «re-» meaning to hold back. The «ie» diphthong is «tye».
p.total.consejo: The sum of everything. The stress falls on the last syllable, «TAL».
p.presenta.consejo: From «presentar». Used with «se» it means to appear at a place, like at a booking.
p.gasto.consejo: From «gastar», to spend. A «gasto» is money that goes out, the opposite of income.
p.adicional.consejo: From «adición», an addition. It is something extra added on top of the agreed price.
p.cobra.consejo: From «cobrar», to charge or collect payment. The «c» before «o» is a «k».
p.finalizar.consejo: From «final», the end. A more formal way to say «terminar».
p.acordado.consejo: From «acordar», to agree. The «-ado» is the past participle, used after «haber».
p.condición.consejo: A requirement that must be met first. The «c» before «o» is «k», and «-ción» is the ending.
